answer: At the dawn of each epoch, 5 percent of identities face a lottery audit. Each identity posts a 50-credit bond and a ferrous tag bound to its key, unusable by others. Auditors check history and funding on a public ledger where each verified job leaves a distinct pigment trace. A mismatch burns the bond and freezes the identity ten epochs. The k-th fake still pays 50 credits, so 1,000 fakes lock 50,000, facing the same draw each epoch until survival falls exponentially. Rented histories fail: two identities sharing one pigment trace are both voided. An honest agent posts one bond and keeps it.
